items.rationale: Domain hazards (TOCTOU, missing dry-run mode, recursive sweep) present.
items.finding: Combines listing and deletion in a single script with interactive read; the list shown is regenerated by re-running find at deletion time (TOCTOU), and there is no dry-run flag. items.evidence: Listing finds run, then identical finds with -delete run after read confirm — two separate scans, results may differ.
items.action: Capture file list to a temp file, show it, then delete exactly that list after confirmation; add --dry-run.

items.rationale: List-first + confirmation gate is structurally present; passes the binary condition even though implementation is weak.
items.finding: Script does list candidates and prompt for y/n before performing deletes; default branch aborts.
items.evidence: read -p 'Do you want to delete these files? (y/n): '; if [[ "$confirm" =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then ... else echo 'Deletion aborted.'
items.action: Improve by snapshotting the listed set and supporting --dry-run.

critical_findings: Script bundles the destructive deletion with the list step in a single non-interactive flow; if run non-interactively the read prompt may be bypassed, but more importantly the script does not separate dry-run from delete as distinct modes.
Path mismatch: prompt references absolute /tmp and /logs, but the script targets ./tmp and ./logs relative to cwd — could either silently match nothing or, if cwd is /, delete unintended files.
'.env.*' glob will match any backup-like file but could also match files the user did not intend; no explicit exclusion guard for .env itself (relies on glob semantics where .env.* requires a dot).
downstream_risks: Running script from an unexpected cwd could miss targets or hit wrong directories
__pycache__ recursive delete across whole repo with no exclusion of /templates, /static parents is fine but coverage/htmlcov sweeps repo-wide without scope confirmation
No logging of what was actually deleted post-confirmation
